message.content:
**Uno – Basic Rules (Standard Edition)** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied after each round when a player goes “out.” | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck: 0–9, Skip, Reverse, Draw Two, Wild, Wild Draw Four.
• Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). On your turn you may:
1. **Play a card** that matches the color, number, or symbol of the top discard.
2. **Play a Wild** (any color) or **Wild Draw Four** (must be played only if you have no matching color).
3. **Draw a card** from the draw pile if you cannot play. If the drawn card can be played immediately, you may do so on the same turn. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips their turn. (Must be challenged if you suspect it was illegal.) | | **Calling “UNO”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. Failure to call UNO when required results in a penalty: the player who missed it must draw two cards. | | **Winning a Round** | A round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring & Next Round** | Add the round’s points to the winner’s total. The next round starts with the winner dealing again. Play continues until someone reaches the target score (usually 500). | --- ### Quick Tips * Keep track of the current color and any pending penalties (e.g., a Draw Two stack). * Use Wild Draw Four strategically—only when you truly have no playable card of the current color. * Challenge a Wild Draw Four if you think the previous player had a legal card; if the challenge fails, you must draw six cards instead of four. Enjoy playing Uno!
